neighbours.label: a comma or ' and'/' but' that joins coordinated items (before the last conjunct)
fire: The hikers crossed rivers, forests, and steep rocky ridges.
The flat was small but bright, quiet, and cheap.
Fire, insects and disease killed most of the old pines.
The path was long, but the view at the top was worth it.
She speaks French, Spanish, and a little Portuguese.
The soup was hot, salty and full of fresh herbs.
Rents rose in the north, the east, and the city centre.
The treatment is slow, but it works for most patients.
quiet: The hikers crossed the river before sunset.
The flat was small for a family of four.
Disease killed most of the old pines in the valley.
The path to the top took the whole afternoon.
She speaks French at home with her grandmother.
The soup was too salty for my taste.
Rents rose sharply in the city centre last year.
The treatment works for most patients within a month.

notes: Card: ' and' x18, ',' x10, ' but' x3 of the top 32, each joining coordinated phrases (similar, yet different, odours; streets, and upper Broadway). Gate-closed echo dominates (65%) and density is ~1%, so near misses will fire weakly. Near misses keep the topic without coordination.
